Artemis Astronauts Return to Earth After Historic Moon Mission

Four astronauts from NASA have returned safely to Earth after completing a historic journey around the Moon as part of the Artemis Program.

The crew was welcomed home in Houston following a nine-day mission that carried them farther from Earth than any human mission in history.

The astronauts traveled aboard Orion spacecraft, which orbited the Moon before beginning its journey back to Earth. The mission marked a major milestone in preparations for future lunar landings and long-term exploration.

During the voyage, the crew conducted tests of spacecraft systems and deep-space navigation while capturing new images of the Moon and Earth from unprecedented distances.

Upon returning home, one astronaut reflected on the mission, saying that seeing Earth from deep space was a reminder that “it’s a special thing to be on Planet Earth.”

The Artemis program aims to establish a sustained human presence on the Moon and eventually prepare for future missions to Mars.

Iran Rejects U.S. Terms as High-Stakes Talks Collapse After 21 Hours

High-level negotiations between the United States and Iran ended without a breakthrough after more than 21 hours of intensive discussions, according to U.S. Vice President JD Vance.

Speaking at a press conference in Islamabad, Pakistan, Vance confirmed that Iranian officials declined to accept the terms presented by the United States during the negotiations.

“The bad news is that we have not reached an agreement,” Vance said, adding that the outcome was likely more damaging for Iran than for the United States.

The talks were part of an urgent diplomatic effort to stabilize a fragile ceasefire and prevent a wider regional escalation following recent hostilities between the two countries.

The U.S. delegation included Vance along with Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and advisor Jared Kushner. Iran was represented by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

According to U.S. officials, the discussions focused heavily on ensuring that Iran would commit to not developing nuclear weapons or obtaining the capability to produce them rapidly.

Vance also confirmed that the U.S. negotiating team maintained constant communication with President Donald Trump throughout the talks, as well as senior administration officials including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Although the negotiations concluded without a deal, Vance stated that the United States left Iran with what he described as its “final and best offer.”

The talks followed a major U.S. military operation targeting Iranian positions earlier this month, a move that significantly escalated tensions across the Middle East.

Resurfaced Democrat Clips on Birthright Citizenship Ignite Online Debate

Old video clips of prominent Democratic leaders discussing birthright citizenship have resurfaced online, triggering renewed political debate as the issue is currently being considered by the U.S. Supreme Court.

One widely circulated clip features former Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid speaking on the Senate floor in 1993 while introducing the Immigration Stabilization Act. At the time, Reid argued that automatic citizenship for children born to undocumented immigrants created incentives for illegal immigration.

Reid stated that rewarding individuals who enter the United States unlawfully with citizenship for their children was a policy he believed needed reform. However, years later in 2018, Reid acknowledged that the proposal had been a mistake and expressed regret over the legislation.

Another resurfaced video shows former U.S. Senator Dianne Feinstein raising concerns in the early 1990s about individuals traveling to the United States to give birth and access public services.

The clips began trending across social media platforms as the United States Supreme Court reviews a major case tied to immigration policy and birthright citizenship. The legal debate centers on the interpretation of the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, which states that all persons born or naturalized in the United States are citizens.

Supporters of reform argue that the amendment has been interpreted too broadly, while critics say altering birthright citizenship would contradict constitutional precedent.

DXCMze-jkDT.content:
Appeals Court Allows Trump’s White House Ballroom Construction to Continue Temporarily

A federal appeals court has ruled that construction on a proposed $400 million White House ballroom project can continue temporarily while legal challenges proceed.

A three-judge panel from the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit instructed a lower court to reconsider an earlier order that had blocked the project. The ruling allows construction to move forward until April 17 while further legal review takes place.

The project, backed by President Donald Trump, involves building a large ballroom complex at the White House site following the demolition of the historic East Wing structure.

Government attorneys argued in court filings that the construction includes significant security upgrades designed to protect the presidential residence and its occupants from potential threats such as drones, ballistic missiles, and biological hazards.

According to the administration, delaying the project would leave the White House complex vulnerable because key security features are integrated into the construction process, including fortified underground facilities such as bomb shelters and medical units.

The lawsuit challenging the project was filed by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which argues that the president exceeded his authority by demolishing and replacing parts of the historic East Wing without congressional approval.

A lower court had previously issued an injunction on March 31 to halt the construction, though that order was temporarily paused to allow the appeal to proceed.

DXCNw7kDp9F.content:
Trump Presses NATO Allies as Canada Finally Hits Defense Spending Target

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has defended Canada’s commitment to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization amid renewed criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump over defense spending by NATO allies.

Speaking at a press conference in Quebec, Carney said Canada is now meeting the alliance’s defense spending benchmark of 2% of gross domestic product — a target Ottawa reached for the first time since the end of the Cold War.

The milestone comes after decades of Canadian defense spending remaining below NATO’s recommended threshold. According to alliance reports, Canada spent roughly 1.01% of GDP on defense in 2014 and remained below 1.5% for most of the following decade before reaching approximately 2.01% in 2025.

Carney emphasized that Canada is fulfilling its alliance responsibilities while also highlighting broader security concerns, including regional tensions involving Iran.

President Trump has repeatedly criticized NATO allies for failing to meet defense spending targets, arguing that the United States carries a disproportionate share of the alliance’s military burden.

Over the past decade, U.S. defense spending has averaged around 3.3% of GDP, significantly higher than most NATO members.

Meanwhile, NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte has acknowledged that pressure from Washington has pushed several alliance members to increase their military spending.

Among NATO countries, Greece and the United Kingdom have consistently ranked among the top contributors relative to their economic size, while several countries — including Canada, Spain, Belgium, and Hungary — have historically spent below the 2% guideline.

Kansas City Clash: Mayor Criticizes State-Controlled Police System

A growing political dispute has emerged in Kansas City over control of the city’s police department, highlighting tensions between local Democratic leadership and Republican officials at the state level.

Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas has sharply criticized the current governance structure of the Kansas City Police Department, describing it as a “colonial system” that limits the city’s ability to control its own policing policies.

Unlike most major U.S. cities, Kansas City does not directly oversee its police force. Instead, the department is governed by a state-appointed board under Missouri law, a structure that dates back more than a century.

Lucas has argued that the system restricts local accountability and undermines the ability of city leadership to implement reforms that reflect the priorities of Kansas City’s diverse population.

Republican lawmakers in Missouri have resisted attempts by city officials to change the arrangement, saying the current system helps maintain oversight and stability in policing.

The dispute reflects a broader political divide between urban Democratic-led cities and conservative state governments across parts of the United States, where debates over policing, governance, and local control have intensified in recent years.

For Kansas City residents, the issue raises fundamental questions about who should ultimately control law enforcement policy — city officials elected by local voters or state authorities.

The breakdown of high-stakes negotiations between the United States and Iran has raised concerns across global markets, with analysts warning that oil prices and borrowing costs could rise sharply in the coming days.

Rising oil prices could also push borrowing costs higher worldwide, increasing pressure on governments and consumers already facing inflation concerns.

Observers now say the world is watching closely for the next move from President Donald Trump as tensions in the region continue to escalate.

The situation underscores the critical role of Middle Eastern energy routes in the global economy and the potential ripple effects if disruptions persist.

Cl94a7sP5KC.content: Here is my first attempt using a 3D sculpting app on my iPad called #NomadSculpt and let me tell you, this stuff is much harder than it looks when you are a complete newbie to using 3D Sculpting applications. But the tutorials that I watched said it’s a fantastic app for people who already know how to do this kind of artwork and they assured me it was a great one to use for people like me. Well, it was tougher than the tutorials made it look, but I fumbled through and managed to finish this little guy. The hardest thing for me was figuring out all the new terminology used in the interface and learning how to use the tools. That gizmo is so difficult to get used to using. LOL! And I wish that the app came with more texture files, environment, and background options. I’m not convinced 3D Art is my thing, but I will do a little more exploring and see if I can turn out something better than this first attempt.

C4RntkDNGpp.content:
International Women's Day.

I am woman… not just today, but every day.

I am courageous, I am creative, I am beautiful…
I am strong, I am independent, I am vivacious…

I am this, this, this, and this…
and that, that, that and that…
The titles are never ending… I am Woman!

Growing up for me, there was no book or instructions on becoming -
Becoming a woman, a mother, a conqueror…
Becoming a teacher, a leader, a friend…
Becoming driven, determined, destined…

and if there was… I didn't read it, nor did I need it.
That would have been the writer's opinion or story of
what a woman is in their perspective. That person's
story or journey could never be my story or journey.

My journey as a woman meant, I chose to walk my own path.
Didn't wanna walk in nobody else's footprints, so I created my own.

Over the years, I grew through… through the pain, the struggles, the frustration and uncertainties, through the tears and the fears.

I had to figure it out, work it out, balance it out.
I prayed, I sought, I cried, I endured… I am Woman!

My image of a woman is defined through God's transformation of me, not through the image of what the world says a woman should be.

Colette Dright

No bake mosaic cake 
This cake is impressive, delicious and easy to assemble. 
کیک موزایکی یخچالی با طرحی زیبا، طعمی فراموش نشدنی و فوق العاده ساده 🌺 دستور فارسی در کامنت 
200 gram whipping cream, 130 gram dark chocolate, 1 teaspoon melted butter, 1 teaspoon orange or lemon rinds, 250 grams graham or plain tea cookies. 
In a large bowl, break the cookies into big chunks ( don't smash them because you want the mosaic look) and set aside. Bring the cream and butter to a boil, turn dawn the heat, cut the chocolate into small pieces and add to the  cream. Mix until chocolate is melted then add the orange rind. Pour the cream and melted chocolate on the cookies. Mix just enough so all the cookies are covered. Do not over mix. Cover the bottoms of a pie or any round mold with stretch plastic. (My mold was 22 centimeter) Place in the fridge for at least 2 hours. Put  your serving dish at rim of the mold and invert the cake. Remove the plastic and decorate with whipped cream and strawberries or any other desired fruits. Refer to other pictures for the preparation stages. #nobakedessert #nobake #easycake #cookiecake#کیک_یخچالی #کیک_خانگی #کیک_شکلاتی_مخصوص #bakers #mosaiccake

Asparagus stew
خورش مارچوبه، غذایی متفاوت و خوشمزه ، و دسر کرم طالبی. دستور فارسی در اولین کامنت 
If you like asparagus, you should definitely try this stew and if you don't like asparagus, this stew will make you change your mind😉
One large onion diced, 500 gram stew meat, 1/2 tsp each turmeric, cumin powder, and coriander powder, 3 cups boiling water, 1 large potato peeled and cut into 2 inch chunks, 2 Tbsp tomato purée, 1 teaspoon chopped garlic, salt and pepper to taste, 6 asparagus sprigs, 2 Tbsp lime or lemons juice. Sauté the onion in two Tbsp oil on medium heat for 3 minutes, add turmeric, cumin and coriander powder and sauté for another minute. Add the meat and mix. Pour 3 cups of boiling water and cover the pot. Lower the heat and let the meat cook until cooked, ( Alternatively use a pressure cooker for fast cooking). Sauté tomato past and garlic in two Tbsp of oil for a few minutes and add to the pot with the potatoes once the meat is cooked. At the end, add the chopped asparagus and lime juice, salt and pepper and let the stew cook only for four more minutes. Enjoy with basmati rice, fresh herbs and assorted pickles.#fane_ashpazi #foodinstagram #ashpazi_shoma #ashpazi_modern #ashpazi #ashpazi_ba_asatid #basaligheha #dinnerideas #stew

Chicken with sour 
Chicken breast with sour grape is an old authentic Persian recipe. It can be served with both eggplants or zucchini. 
500 g chicken breast cut into long strips, 1 medium onion diced, 6 zucchini, 2 eggs, 1 cup bread crumbs, 1/2 tsp each, paprika, black pepper, coriander powder, lemon pepper, 1 tsp salt, 1 Tbsp liquid saffron, 1 Tbsp tomato paste. 
Cut zucchini's in half and make long cuts all the way down each half. ( look at the pictures and video clip). Dip each half into egg and then drench in bread crumbs. Set aside. 
Place the onion and 2 Tbsp oil in a pan on medium heat and stir for about 5 minutes. Add the spices and chicken. Let the chicken change colors on all sides ( about 10 minutes) be careful not to burn the onions. Add tomato paste and one and half cup boiling water to the pan, cover and cook for about 15 minutes. Add the sour grape and cook for another 5 to 10 minutes without lid.Meanwhile fry the zucchini in oil and drain on paper towel. 
Arrange the zucchini and chicken on a platter and serve with basmati rice and fresh herbs.

Fig cup cakes, it is as tasty as it is beautiful. Please turn the page. 
کیک انجیر خوشمزه و متفاوت😋دستور فارسی در کامنت, لطفا عکسها را ورق بزنید.
3 eggs, 2/3 cup sugar, 1 tsp of each lemon rind and vanilla, half cup of each milk, Greek yogurt and oil, 4 Tbsp desiccated coconut, 2 cups flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 6 to 7 figs(slice 3 of them into rounds and 3 cut dice into small pieces)
Sift flour and baking powder twice, set aside. Beat eggs, sugar, rind and vanilla for at least 3 minutes on high until cream in color and double in size. Add milk, yogurt, and oil and mix for another minutes. Mix diced figs and coconut. 
Fold in the flour in three batches using a wooden or silicone spoon. 
Heat the oven at 200 centigrade or 400 Fahrenheit. Place liners in a cup cake mold and fill each liner two thirds. Place the tray in oven for 6 minutes, then while cup cakes are in the oven, place one fig round in the middle of each cup cake. 
Lower temperature to 180 C or 350 F and bake for another 15 to 17 minutes. Test with a toothpick. Let the cakes cool and decorate with powdered sugar or pistachios. *Baking cupcakes for 6 minute at high temperature would cause the cakes to rise rapidly and to allow fig rounds to stay in the middle. This will make 12 to 14 cupcakes #fig_cupcakes #figcake #fig #کاپ_کیک_انجیر #کیک_انجیر #انجیر #مافین_انجیر #bakers #caketime

CGAnP1vB144.content:
Mango mouse pie
پای موس انبه، دستور فارسی در کامنت
For the tart shell: 150 g or one cup flour, 1 tablespoon powdered sugar, 80 g cold butter, one egg yolk, 3 tablespoons cold water, mix flour and sugar, cut the butter into small cubes and in a food processor pulse with the flour and sugar, add the yolk, and cold water and pulse until the dough forms a ball. Sprinkle flour on the table and open the though to the size of your tart mold. My mold was 30 by 10 centimeters or 13" by 4 inches. Fit the dough inside the mold. Make several holes in the dough using a fork. Place a wax paper on top of the dough and place uncooked beans or pie wights on the paper and bake in the pre warmed oven at 350 F or 180 C for 15 minutes then take the beans and the paper out and bake for another 10 minutes. Set aside to cool. 
For the filling: 3/4 cup full fat milk, 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tsp agar agar powder, 2 Tbsp corn starch dissolved in 1/4 cup milk, 1 cup mango purée from 2 fresh mangoes. Bring milk and sugar to a boil add agar agar powder and stir constantly until dissolved ( about 2 minutes), add mango purée and dissolved corn starch. Stir until smooth. Lower temperature and let it simmer for 2 minutes. Pour the mixture over the tart and let it cool completely. Once set, decorate with whipping cream, nuts, and fresh flowers. * instead of agar agar you can use 2 Tbsp gelatin dissolved in 1/4 cup cold milk and once bloomed add to the heated milk sugar mix and follow the rest of the recipe. #mangomouse#mouse#mangotart#tart #تارت #تارت_انبه #انبه #shirini #shikdesser#deserhome1#desere_irani

CGl0Sc_hd9W.content:
Dill sourdough 
نان ساور با شوید
80% hydration, 35 g dark Rye flour, 70 g whole wheat flour, 382 g bread flour, 2 Tablespoons dry dill, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 380 g water, 98 g active starter, 10 g salt
Mix all the flours, dill, cumin and water. Cover with a towel and Let sit for 2 hours at room temperature. Mix in the starter and fold the dough for 4 minutes while in the bowl. Cover and let sit for 30 minutes. Mix in the salt and fold for another 4 minutes. Cover the bowl with the towel and let rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. Laminate the dough by wetting the work surface and hands, stretch to a big rectangle and fold on itself. Place the dough in a clean bowl, cover with towel and rest for 4 hours while Stretch and fold the dough on itself every 30 minutes. After 4 hours, dust the workplace with flour, take the dough out and fold again on itself. Dust the bread basket with rice flour and place the dough top side dawn in the basket. Cover with towel and rest overnight in fridge. Next day heat the oven with a Dutch oven inside at 500 F for at least 30 minutes. Take the dough out of the basket, score your design with a sharp blade, slip parchment paper under the bough and place in the hot dutch oven.
Bake at 500 F for 30 minutes, remove the lid, lower temperature to 475F and bake for another 15 to 20 minutes.

کوکی رز و پسته برای تولد خاتم الانبیا محمد مصطفی (ص) 🌹دستور فارسی در کامنت 
This cookie has a mild but subtle aroma of rose with an inviting appearance. 
125 g butter at room temp, 80 g powdered sugar, 1 egg, 1 tablespoons rose water, 200 g flour, 30 g corn starch, pinch of salt, 2 tsp powdered Rose petals, half cup powdered raw pistachios. Beat butter and sugar for 5 minutes on medium, add the egg, rose powder and rose water. Beat for another 2 minutes. Sift flour, corn starch and salt twice and add to the mix using a silicon or wooden spoon. Once flour is incorporated mix in the powered pistachios. Wrap the dough in Plastic and let rest in fridge for one to two hours. Heat the oven to 350F or 180C
Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.
Open the dough between two sheets of plastic to 4 or 5 mm thickness. Cut the cookies using your a round 2" cookie cutter. Then cut the middle of each cookie using a small cutter. Bake cookies for 12 To 14 minutes depending on your oven temperature. To decorate, melt good quality white chocolate on a double boiler or microwave and brush a part of the cookie. Sprinkle dry rose Petals, slivered pistachios or gojis berries on chocolate. Note: you can find aromatic rose powder, rose  petals and rose water in middle eastern or Indian stores. #rosecookies #rosecookie #pistachiocookies #pistachiocookie #christmascookies #festivecookies #شیرینی_گل_محمدی #شیرینی_رینگ_آجیلی #شبرینی_عید

Raspberry tiramisu 
تیرامیسوی رازبری، دستور فارسی در کامنت 
One large package (about 30) tiramisu, one pound raspberry, 1/2 cup sugar, 200 g mascarpone cheese, 200 g whipping cream, 1 teaspoon vanilla powder or extract,
8" round or square ring. 
Place raspberries and sugar in a pan on medium heat, let raspberries cook for about 10 minutes. Using a blender puréed raspberries and pass them through a sieve.
Toss the seeds and let the juice cool.
Place the ring inside your serving dish. Arrange ladyfingers like picket fence using the ring as support. Cover the bottom with ladyfingers as tightly as possible breaking them as needed to fit the corners. Whip the cream, sugar and vanilla until stiff then add mascarpone and mix. Using a pastry bag, cover the bottom layer of ladyfingers with the cream mix. For the Second layer dip each Ladyfingers in raspberry syrup and place on top of the cream mix. Cover with cream and continue layering until the cake reaches the top of the standing ladyfingers.
Top the cake with cream mix, then a thin layer of raspberry syrup. Decorate with whole raspberries and cream mix. Let the cake stay in fridge over night or at least 12 hours. Remove the ring and wrap a red ribbons around the cake. #rasberry #tiramisucake #tiramisu #rasberrytiramisu #caketime #تیرامیسو #کیک_خانگی #کیک #shirini #ashpazi_shoma

Spinach Swiss roll 
رولت اسفناج ، دستور فارسی در کامنت 
4 eggs, 3/4 cup sugar, 3 Tbsp spinach juice ( from 2 cups of blended and squeezed fresh spinach leaves),3/4 cup flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 
Place a parchment paper in a 30 by 40 centimeter tray. Turn the oven to 180 centigrade or 350 Fahrenheit. 
Separate the egg whites from yolks. Beat the whites until foamy then add half the sugar one spoon at the time. Keep beating until soft peaks form. Set aside in the fridge. In another bowl beat the yolks with the rest of the sugar until cream color and double in size,then add the spinach juice. Mix the flour and backing powder and sift twice, then add it the yolk mix using a wooden spoon. Finally add the whites in three batches. Mix carefully not to deflate the mix. Pour the batter in the tray and spread. Drop the tray on the counter a few times to get rid of all the air bubbles. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes. Let the cake cool and turn to peel the paper Then wrap the cake in a clean parchment paper and roll. Let the cake cool. Unwrap the cake and cover with cream, fruits or nuts. Wrap and decorate with fruits or flowers. Coconut cake : simply delicious and easy to bake. 
کیک نارگیل بسیار خوشمزه و ساده: دستور فارسی در کامنت 
Spray a 23 centimeters (9") circular mold ( with at least 3" depth) with non stick oil and turn the oven to 350 F or 180 C. You need: 4 eggs separated, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup coconut milk or regular milk, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 1/2 cup liquid oil, 1 cup shredded unsweetened coconut, 2 cups flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp salt
Sift flour, baking powder and salt and set aside. 
Beat the egg whites with half the sugar until soft peaks form, set the bowl in the fridge.
In a separate bowl beat the rest of the sugar with egg yolks for 3 to 4 minutes until creamy, add vanilla. Heat the coconut milk until hot and pour on the egg yolk while beating on high. Add coconut flakes. Gradually add the flour. Batter will be stiff. 
Mix in the egg whites in three batches with a  Wooden spoon in a circular motion. Pour the batter in the mold and bake for about 40 minutes. Once cooled, remove from the mold and decorate with powdered sugar. 
I cut out 4 strips of paper and laid them over cake( the way you cut a pizza), sprinkled powder sugar and then removed the papers.

Mini tarts: For crust: 125 g butter at room temp, 2 egg yolks, 1 tsp vanilla, 20 g powdered baking milk, 200 g flour ( for the chocolate crust you need additional 2 Tbsp cocoa butter)
Beat butter and powdered sugar on high for 3 minutes, add the yolks and vanilla, beat for another minute, then add the powdered milk and beat for another minute. Mix in the flour by hand. Do not over mix. Wrap the dough in a plastic and let rest in the fridge for at least one hour. Remover from the fridge and let it sit at room temp so it would be pliable. Open the dough between two plastic to 2 to 3 millimeter thick. Use the tart mold to cut the dough, place the cuts inside the mold. ( see the pictures) Using fork make holes inside the tarts. For chocolate, fruit and nut tarts, cook the shells first. Place several raw beans inside the tarts to prevent them from puffing up. Cook at 170 C or 325 F preheated oven for 12 to 14 minutes. Let them cool completely. Use a toothpick to release the edges of the tarts from the molds and fill with your favorite filling. I brushed inside some with strawberry jam, then piped whipping cream in each, toped with a fresh raspberry. For chocolate heat up 200 milliliter whipping cream, add 200 g semisweet chopped chocolate and 1 Tbsp orange rind. Mix until chocolate melts. Pour inside the tarts and decorate as you wish. For the nut filling, in a pot on medium heat mix 50 g honey, 30 g whipping cream, 20 g butter and 1 teaspoon liquid saffron. Stir until liquid is hot then add 100 g slivered almonds. Fill the tarts with this mix, put the filled tarts back in the molds. Put them in oven and grill them on high for 2 to 3 minutes. Let them cool completely and remove from the molds. #minitarts #mini_tarts #tart #fancysweets #تارت #مینی_تارت #شیرینی_عید #شیرینی_خونگی #شیرینی_بوتیکی #shirinneshat #

Financiers are petite cakes with crispy top and medium density. They are high in protein due to egg whites. The unique taste is due to the brown butter.
60 g flour, 60 g almond meal, a pinch of salt, 120 g powdered sugar, 5 egg whites, 1 drop almond oil or 1 tsp almond extract, 100g unsalted butter, 1/2 tsp baking powder almond slices for garnish. 
Place the butter in a small pot on medium heat until it melts, lower the heat and let the butter get golden color, be careful it does not burn. It takes about 7 minutes. Use a small fine mesh to separate the liquid butter from the brown solids. You only need the clear liquid. While the butter cools down, mix flour, almond meal, salt, baking powder and sugar in a bowl. Sift once and set aside. In a different bowl, using a hand whisk, mix the egg whites and almond oil a little bit. Add the whites to the dry ingredients with a hand whisk. Then add the butter in three to four batches and gently mix. Cover the batter with plastic and let it rest in the fridge for at least 2 hours or up to 12 hours. 
Heat the oven at 200 C or 390 F butter the cups of a financier mold or muffin mold generously. Decide the chilled batter equally among the cups. Garnish the top with slices of almonds. Bake at 200 C for 10 minutes for cakes to rise, then lower the temp to 180C or 350 F and bake for another 15 minutes or until a tester comes out clean.#financier#petitcake #frenchcakes #minicakes #شیرینی_بوتیکی #shirini #کیک_خانگی #فینانسیه #kadbanoo_basalighe #persianbaking #teatime☕️

کوکی مرمری زیبا کمی کار داره ولی به زحمتش می ارزه. دستور از دوست هنرمندم @barane78 
1 egg, 175 g flour, 60 g powdered sugar,35 g oil, half tea spoon or 2 g baking powder, half teaspoon vanilla or cardamom powder, one drop red food coloring.
Sift flour and baking powder and set aside. In a bowl mix the egg, sugar, on low speed until sugar is dissolved, (just a minute), add vanilla and oil and mix just until incorporated. Add the flour and mix by hand. Divide the dough in half, place each half in a plastic and let rest in the freezer for half an our. Mix one half with food coloring then mix the colored and non colored dough together gently for a marble effect. Don't over mix. (Refer to the pictures). Roll the dough out between two stretch wrap to 3 to 4 millimeters. Use any silicone stencil to creat pattern on the dough and cut them with your favorite cuter. Bake on parchment paper at 180C or 385F for 13 to 15 minutes.
Don't over back. Recipe from @barane78

Pistachio jam cookies 
شیرینی پسته ایی مربایی 
عید سعید غدیر مبارک 🌹
The taste of this beautiful cookie is sure to please you such that you can't just have one.😊
200 g Finley crushed pistachios, 200 g unsalted butter at Room temp, 150 g powdered sugar, 2 cups rice flour, 2 egg yolk, couple drops of almond extract, 2 tablespoons baking matcha or 2 drops of green food coloring ( if you wish ) 
Beat sugar and butter for 3 minutes, add egg yolk and almond extract, and matcha or food coloring and beat for another minute. Add the flour and mix for another minute. Lastly use a wooden or silicone spoon to mix in the nuts. Do not over mix because the dough will start to produce oil. Wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate for at least two hours. Open the dough between two of parchment or stretch wrap to a 0.5 centimeters. Use your favorite Cooke cutter to cut the desired shape. My cutter had indentation inside. Bake at 350 F or 170C preheated oven for about 12 minutes. If you over bake, the green color will be lost. Use your favorite jam to fill the inside of the cookie or between two cookies like a sandwich. Enjoy.

Fan cookies
This cookie is sure to impress everyone.
کوکی بادبزن زیبا و خوشمزه
200 g flour, 3 Tbsp corn starch, 100 g softened butter, 70 g powdered sugar, 1 egg yolk, 1 teaspoons vanilla. For the glaze; 1 egg yolk, 1 tsp dark cocoa powder, 1 tsp milk. Beat sugar and butter at high for 5 minutes, add one egg yolk and vanilla and beat for another 2 minutes. Replace 3 Tbsp of flour with 3 Tbsp starch. Sift the flour a couple times then add it to the batter using a wooden spoon or your hands. The final dough should be soft and non sticky. Wrap the dough in plastic and refrigerate for one hour. Then open the dough between two stretch wrap to a thickness of 5 millimeter. Using a scalloped cookie cutter cut out cookies and then using a knife cut them in half. Mix all the glaze ingredients and brush the cookies with it. Then using a knife make lines on the cookies resembling a fan. Bake the cookies at 180 C or 350 for 10 to 12 minutes. Pumpkin pancakes پن کیک کدو حلوایی  2 Cups All Purpose Flour, 1 Tbsp Baking Powder, 1 tsp Salt,1½ tsp Ground Cinnamon, ½ tsp Ground Ginger, ½ Teaspoon Ground Nutmeg, ¼ Cup Brown Sugar, ¼ Cup Granulated Sugar, 1 Teaspoon Vanilla Extract,1 Cup Pumpkin Puree, 2 Large Eggs, 4 Tablespoons Butter Melted, 1 ½ Cups Milk
Mix flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg and put aside. In a different bowl, mix the rest of the ingredients. Pour the wet ingredients over the dry ingredients and whisk to combine. Batter will be lumpy, don't over mix. 
Heat the griddle or pan then coat it with nonstick spray or a little butter and pour 1/4 to 1/3 cup of batter. Cook about 4 minutes on medium per side. Serve with fresh fruits, nuts or whipped cream. * eliminate white sugar if you want to serve it with syrup.

parfait cake 
کیک پارافیت پر میوه و بدون فر
This is a no bake desert that is easy, beautiful and delicious. 
150 g tea biscuits, 1 1/2 cup diced strawberries, 1 1/2 cup diced mango, half cup kiwis (optional), 1/2 cup mini chocolate chips, 1/2 cup nut of your choice( I used pistachios), 400 g whipping cream, 1/4 cup cream cheese, 100 g white chocolate. 
Line a loaf pan with stretch plastic. 
Break biscuits into small chunks, add all the fruits, chocolate chips and nuts. Melt the white chocolate on top of a double broiled set aside to cool slightly. 
In a different bowl, Whip the cream until stiff, add cream cheese and melted chocolate then add the biscuit fruit mix.
Transfer the mix to the mold. Cover the mold  with plastic and freeze the cake for 3 to 4 hours. Invert the mold in a dish and pull off the plastic. Decorate with fruits and nuts.

Vegetarian eggplant halim, حلیم بادنجان بدون گوشت
1 kilogram or 2 pounds eggplants, 1/2 cup rice, 1/2 cup whey or Greek yogurt,  1/2 cup crushed walnuts, 5 garlic cloves smashed,
2 medium onions peeled and thinly sliced, 2 Tbsp dry and crushed mint leaves, 1/2 tsp each turmeric, cinnamon, 1 tsp each salt and pepper (or to taste)، 1 Tbsp liquid saffron. Make several holes in eggplants and grill them until they are soft and cooked. The best way to grill them is to use charcoal to get the smoky flavor or use store bought roasted eggplants.(You can also peel and fry them on both sides). 
While eggplants are cooking, in a small pot boil the rice with one and half cups of water, a pinch of salt and a little oil until the rice is completely cooked and no liquid is left, set aside. Note, you may need to add a bit more water to insure the rice is cooked and soft.
After grilling, peel them while still hot. Place the eggplants and rice in a bowl and smash them. In a small pan sauté dry mint with 1 Tbsp oil for just 1 minute, set aside. In a large pan on medium heat fry the onions in 3 Tbsp oil for about 10 minutes then add the garlic and all the spices and fry for another minute. Add the smashed eggplants and continue to sauté the eggplants for about 10 minutes. Place the mix in a large bowl and add the 1/4 of whey, half the fried onions, walnuts, saffron, and salt and pepper. Adjust the salt to taste.Then place the mix in a serving dish and decorate with dry mint, herbs, fried onion and liquid whey.

Persimmon galette
‎ گالت خرمالو، بسیار راحت و بسیار خوشمزه 
This is a delicious dessert you can make under an hour. Use a store bought pie crust, or make your own. Choose several firm persimmons and using a mandolin cut them into slices. Roll out the crust and spread just a couple spoons of mascarpone cheese in the middle of the crust. Leave 2" without cheese on the periphery. Sprinkle 1/2 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp brown sugar on the cream cheese. Arrange persimmon rounds in a circular form in the middle of the crust. Fold the sides of crust to cover the edges of the fruit. Brush the crust with egg yolk, (don't brush the persimmons). Bake in a pre warm oven at 380F or 180 C for about 25 to 30 minutes depending on your oven temperature. Warm up 2 Tbsp apricot jam in the microwave, Take the galette out and brush the fruit and the crust with warm apricot and sprinkle with pistachios.

CbhDp03ugxc.content:
Three different cookies from one dough 
سه نوع شیرینی خوشمزه با یک خمیر پایه
400 g flour, 200 g butter at room temp, 140g powdered sugar, 2 egg yolks, 1 teaspoon vanilla, 60 ml oil, 30 g finely ground pistachios, 30 g ground almonds, 14g cocoa powder, one drop almond extract, one drop green food gel, two drops liquid saffron(optional), 2 Tbsp berry jam 
Beat butter and sugar for 3 minutes at high, add egg yolks, oil and vanilla. Beat for another minute. Mix in the flour in two batches by hand until a nice pliable dough is formed. Divid the dough to three equal portions. To one portion add pistachios and one drop green food gel, to the second dough add almonds and one drop almond extract and saffron, to the third dough add cocoa powder. Do not over mix the doughs. Apple Turnover
The easiest, delicious, professional looking pastry anyone can make in 30 minutes. 
For eight 5" by 5" or 13 centimeter pastry you will need, eight 5" puff pastry squares, 2 medium apple peeled and cut into small pieces, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 20 gram butter, 2 Tbsp walnut pieces. For the top you need to mix 1 egg plus 1 Tbsp milk( I added a bit of saffron) and few almond slices If desired.
Place butter, apples, sugar and cinnamon, and walnuts in a small pot and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, set aside to cool. Dust the work surface with a little flour and assemble the pastry by placing about 2 Tbsp of the apple mixture in the middle of the pastry squares. Brush two sides of the pastry with the egg wash and attach the ends to form a triangle. Press the edges well with a fork. Make 3 cuts on top of the pastry for steam to scape. Place the assembled pastries on a parchment covered tray and let them rest in the fridge for 20 minutes. Then brush them with egg wash sprinkle with Almond slices if desired.
Heat the oven to 390 F or 200 C 
Cook the pastries for 20 to 23 minutes until nicely gold and flaky. Once baked you can brush the top of the hot pastries with apricot jam to give it a nice glaze. #appleturnover #applepie #applepastry #پای_سیب #شیرینی_سیب_دارچین  دستور فارسی در کامنت

The recipe for this Swiss roll, is the best one in my opinion : 4 Egg yolks room temp, 3/4 cup sugar, 40 ml(1/4 cup), 40 ml (1/4) cup oil, 1 tsp Vanilla extract, 3/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup corn starch, 1 tsp lemon juice or vinegar. For the filling we need, 125 ml Whipping cream, 20 g sugar and 1 tsp vanilla. For cover: 200 g white chocolate and color of your choice. Fruit of your choice is optional, I added  a 1/2 cup of raspberries 
Separate the egg yolks from the egg whites. Add vinegar to the egg whites and beat until foamy, gradually add half the sugar and keep beating until stiff. In a different bowl beat the egg yolks with the rest of the sugar and vanilla until pale in color, add the flour and cornstarch to the egg yolks in two batches. Incorporate the egg whites. Be careful not to deflate the egg whites. Line an 18 by 13 inch baking sheet with parchment paper. Pour the butter and even it out using a spatula. Tap the tray several times on the counter so all the air bubbles are out. Bake at 165 C or 325F for 25 minutes. Let the cake cool completely. Peel off the parchment and spread it with whipping cream, which you have beaten with sugar and vanilla. Cut a clean piece of bubble wrap the size of your roll. Melt the chocolate. Take 2 Tbsp of the melted chocolate and color it with the color you like. 
Spread the colored chocolate over the bubble wrap in a random pattern. Then cover the whole sheet with melted white chocolate. Wait a few minutes for chocolate to set then wrap it around the roll and press down to ensure the chocolate sticks tightly to the cake. Let it sit for about 10 minutes and carefully peel off the wrap. Enjoy.

Mango tiramisu  so delicious everyone would ask you for the recipe 🌺
Mango tiramisu 
¾ cup mango pulp, 200 to 225 g mascarpone cheese, 1/4 cup sugar, 1/4 cup of granulated sugar, 1 teaspoon vanilla extract, 2 cups heavy cream, 260 g Ladyfingers or enough to fill your dish
Topping
⅔ cup mango pulp, mango peels, mint leaves and fresh flowers. 
The above is for a nine inch square dish. I used a 9 by 11 inch dish and doubled the ingredients. 
In a bowl, whisk together the mascarpone cheese, sugar, and vanilla extract for about one minute, or until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whisk heavy cream until stiff peaks form. Carefully fold one-third of the whipped cream into the mascarpone mixture. Gradually fold in the remaining whipped cream, being careful not to overmix.
Once the filling is prepared, pour in 1/2 cup of the mango pulp and gently fold. Set aside.
Then, pour the remaining pulp into a shallow dish. Dip each ladyfinger into the pulp then arrange them in a single layer at the bottom of your serving dish.
Spread half of the mango mascarpone filling over the ladyfingers and smooth the surface. Add another layer of dipped ladyfingers, followed by the remaining filling. Smooth the top, cover the dish with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight for the best results.
Just before serving, pour the remaining mango pulp over the tiramisu and smooth it out. Then add mango roses to the corner of the dish and garnish with mint leaves as shown. Original recipe with some modifications from @simshomekitchen #mangotiramisu  #fruitcake #تیرامیسو #انبه

DS1crXDEY5R.content:
ژله ویترینی 
Do not let this flower Jell-O intimidate you. It is easy to make. You just need a flower silicon mold. To make the flowers you need one cup or 200 mL milk, 50 mL heavy whipping cream, 50 g sugar, 2 tablespoon unflavored gelatin powder, half a teaspoon vanilla, a few drops of red color. Mix all the above and dissolved gelatin using  bain_marie method. I put the bowl on top a boiling kettle. Lightly brush your flower mold with oil. Fill up the mold with the above liquid. Placed in the freezer for 15 minutes, then carefully take the flower out of the mold. It takes about two hours to make nine flowers. Once you have all your flower start making  the first layer. Mix one pack of aloe vera Jell-O or unflavored gelatin with 1 1/2 cup hot water, steer to dissolve the Jell-O completely. Pour 10 tablespoon of the clear gelatin mix at the bottom of your mold.  Put the mold in the fridge for 10 minutes. Then place all flowers face down on the clear Jell-O. If you like sprinkle a few slivered pistachio or mint leaves on the side of the flowers.. carefully pour the rest of the clear Jell-O on top and around the flowers and place in the fridge for 15 minutes. For the last layer. Dissolve one pack of strawberry Jell-O with 2 tablespoon unflavored gelatin, in one and a half cup of hot water. In a food processor place the dissolved gelatin, 120 g of tea biscuits 1 teaspoon vanilla, 200 mL heavy cream and one cup milk. Mix until smooth. Pour this mixture on top of the clear Jell-O in the mold. Break about 100 g tea biscuits into big chunks and add to this last layer. Let it rest in the fridge for five hours or overnight. Dip the mold in warm water to take out the jello. #jello #jellocake #ژله_ویترینی #ژله_مجلسی #ژله

DQmFY3jES-o.content:
“He had begun to believe this because for him the universe — his universe - was indeed fast turning into information. Once God started talking to him he never seemed to stop. I don’t think they report that in the Bible.
Journal entry #37. Thoughts of the Brain are experienced by us as arrangements and rearrangements — change — in a physical universe; but in fact it is really information and information-processing which we substantialize. We do not merely see its thoughts as objects, but rather as the movement, or, more precisely, the placement of objects: how they become linked to one another. But we cannot read the patterns of arrangement; we cannot extract the information in it - i.e. it as information, which is what it is. The linking and relinking of objects by the Brain is actually a language, but not a language like ours (since it is addressing itself and not someone or something outside itself).
Fat kept working this particular theme over and over again, both in his journal and in his oral discourse to his friends. He felt sure the universe had begun to talk to him. Another entry in his journal reads:
#36. We should be able to hear this information, or rather narrative, as a neutral voice inside us. But something has gone wrong. All creation is a language and nothing but a language, which for some inexplicable reason we can’t read outside and can’t hear inside. So I say, we have become idiots. Something has happened to our intelligence. My reasoning is this: arrangement of parts of the Brain is a language. We are parts of the Brain; therefore we are language. Why,
then, do we not know this? We do not even know what we are, let alone what the outer reality is of which we are parts. The origin of the word “idiot” is the word “private.” Each of us has become private, and no longer shares the common thought of the Brain, except at a subliminal level. Thus our real life and purpose are conducted below our threshold of consciousness.
To which I personally am tempted to say, Speak for yourself, Fat.”

Valis
Philip K. Dick

C8_El6tRwvf.content: Here’s a very obscure piece of Beatles history. Elephant’s Memory was a hard rock band out of NYC in the early 70s. They were also John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s back up band for several years and appeared on some of John’s earlier solo albums. John & Yoko produced their 1972 album, and John even appears on several tracks on guitar and vocals. The album was released on The Beatles Apple records. It’s never been released on CD and is currently out of print. Great stuff and a good example of early hard rock. Very cool album. #vinylcollection #johnlennon #applerecords #1972 #elephantsmemoryband #elephantsmemoryplasticonoband

CEXQjpHAoml.content:
Louie was a guardian. When Lou was a hair short of 2 years old, he chased intruders out of my apartment as I slept. I awoke to his loud barking and the fearful fading screams of the would be intruders. As I peered out the door, Lou was at the top stair, hair up, barking mad. I stepped on to the porch to see an old Cadillac peeling out of the parking area. “Good boy Lou”, I mumbled. His hair dropped, he ran inside, laid on the couch, looked at me like nothing had happened. “Let’s go back to bed” i said. He jumped off the couch and ran into the bedroom. I locked the front door and turned off the lights.

RIP Lou

Pastéis de Nata at Manteigaria, Lisbon

Manteigaria is one of Lisbon’s most renowned spots for pastéis de nata, Portugal’s iconic custard tart. These flaky, golden pastries feature a rich, creamy custard filling encased in buttery, crisp puff pastry, baked to perfection with a signature caramelized top.

DDl-jRYR4eC.content:
📍🇵🇹 Lisbon, Portugal

The Tower of Belém 

An iconic landmark located on the northern bank of the Tagus River in Lisbon, Portugal. Built between 1514 and 1520 during the reign of King Manuel I, the tower originally served as part of the city’s defensive system and as a ceremonial gateway to Lisbon. Designed in the Manueline style, it features ornate maritime motifs, intricate carvings, and unique elements like armillary spheres, ropes, and crosses of the Order of Christ.

The tower is closely associated with Portugal’s Age of Exploration, symbolizing the country’s maritime prowess and the voyages of discovery that expanded its influence globally. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983, it is celebrated for its historical significance, architectural beauty, and stunning location, offering visitors panoramic views of the river and surrounding area.

The coastlines of Albufeira, Lagos, and the Algarve as a whole are renowned for their dramatic beauty and diversity. Albufeira’s coastline is marked by golden sandy beaches, limestone cliffs, and hidden coves, ideal for swimming and sunbathing. Lagos boasts a more rugged and picturesque shoreline, featuring iconic rock formations like those at Ponta da Piedade, sea caves, and turquoise waters. Across the Algarve, you’ll find a mix of lively resort beaches and secluded, pristine stretches of sand, all framed by breathtaking cliffs and the clear waters of the Atlantic Ocean.

DDp2HUqRDFC.content:

Small restaurants on dimly lit streets have me in an absolute chokehold. Is there anything better? Probably. But they are special. I was originally planning on being in Algarve for 2-days and then just stopping in Évora on my way to Coimbra. However, it was the offseason along the southern coast and there wasn’t a lot going on, so I decided to leave a day early and spend the night in Évora; excellent decision. 

Évora, located in Portugal’s Alentejo region, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its rich history, well-preserved architecture, and vibrant culture. 

📍 Carne de Porco à Alentejana is a classic Portuguese dish combining marinated pork, clams, and a savory sauce made with garlic, paprika, and white wine. Originating from the Alentejo region, it reflects the area’s culinary heritage by blending land and sea flavors. 

📍 Grilled sausages in Évora are a quintessential part of the city’s culinary experience, reflecting the traditions of Alentejo. Known for smoky, rustic flavors, the sausages are crafted from local pork, seasoned with garlic, paprika, and regional herbs. 

📍 Queijo de Ovelha Curado is a delicacy in Alentejo. Made from rich sheep’s milk, this cheese is aged to develop its firm texture and bold, nutty flavor. Its rind may vary from smooth to rustic, while the interior is creamy and dense. 

📍Bolo de Mel de Évora is a traditional dessert from Portugal’s Alentejo region, celebrated for its rich flavors and rustic preparation. This honey-based cake combines the region’s agricultural, including local honey, olive oil, and spices like cinnamon, often enhanced with nuts such as almonds or walnuts.

📍Ruby Port is a sweet, fortified wine from Portugal, known for its vibrant red color and flavors of ripe berries, cherries, and plums. It is aged in large barrels to preserve its fresh, fruity profile and is typically served slightly chilled. Ruby Port is a classic pairing for chocolate desserts, berry-based treats, or nutty pastries, enhancing their richness with its balanced sweetness and bold flavor.

DD7LAqpqmjZ.content:
📍🇲🇦 Fés, Morocco 

The Chouara Tannery in Fés, Morocco, is one of the city’s most iconic landmarks and a testament to its centuries-old leatherworking tradition. Established in the 11th century, it is the largest and oldest tannery in Fes and operates much as it did during medieval times. The tannery is located in the heart of the Fes el-Bali medina, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and features a vibrant array of stone vats filled with natural dyes and solutions.

The leather tanning process begins with raw hides, which are cleaned and softened using a mixture of water and lime. Workers then dye the leather using natural pigments such as saffron, indigo, and henna. The process is labor-intensive, performed entirely by hand, and produces high-quality leather that is crafted into bags, shoes, and other goods sold in the surrounding souks.

Visitors can observe the tannery from nearby terraces, where the sight of colorful dye pits and the scent of the process create an unforgettable sensory experience. Despite its pungency, the Chouara Tannery remains a must-see for its authentic glimpse into Morocco’s cultural heritage.

Switzerland is a multilingual country with distinct linguistic regions that reflect its cultural diversity. The nation is primarily divided into three main language sectors: the German-speaking region, which is the largest and covers central and eastern Switzerland, including cities like Zurich, Bern, and Basel; the French-speaking region in the west, known as Romandy, which includes Geneva, Lausanne, and Neuchâtel; and the Italian-speaking region in the south, primarily located in the canton of Ticino and parts of southern Graubünden. While German is spoken by about 60% of the population, French is spoken by around 20–25%, and Italian by about 8%. This regional breakdown influences food, education, media, government, and daily life, with each area maintaining its linguistic and cultural identity within a cohesive federal framework.

Bologna, Italy, known as “La Grassa” (The Fat One), is a historic and culinary gem in the Emilia-Romagna region. With medieval towers, red-hued porticoes, and one of the world’s oldest universities—founded in 1088—Bologna has long been a center of learning and culture. DK7LIp3K7uq.content:

Bologna, a historic city in northern Italy’s Emilia-Romagna region, is renowned for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant food scene, and one of the oldest universities in the world. Founded by the Etruscans and later expanded under Roman rule, Bologna became an influential medieval city, especially after the establishment of the University of Bologna in 1088. This institution attracted scholars from across Europe and helped shape Bologna into a hub of intellectual and legal thought. During the Renaissance, the city flourished artistically and economically, despite periods of Papal control. Bologna’s well-preserved medieval architecture, such as the Two Towers (Asinelli and Garisenda), its arcaded streets, and red-tiled roofs, continue to reflect its nickname “La Rossa” (The Red), symbolizing both its architecture and leftist political history. Today, Bologna blends academic tradition, culinary excellence, and vibrant urban life, standing as a testament to its enduring legacy.

Venice, founded over 1,500 years ago on a lagoon of islands, developed a rich culinary tradition shaped by its role as a powerful maritime republic and gateway between East and West. As Venetian merchants brought back spices, grains, and exotic ingredients from across the globe, these influences blended with the city’s local bounty—especially seafood from the Adriatic. A beloved expression of this heritage is cicchetti, bite-sized snacks traditionally served in bacari (rustic wine bars) since at least the 13th century. Originally enjoyed by workers and traders seeking a quick, affordable bite with wine, cicchetti include classics like baccalà mantecato (creamed cod), fried calamari, or crostini topped with salumi and vegetables. Today, this tradition remains central to Venetian life, offering a flavorful, social way to experience the city’s history through its food.

We did 8 miles in Corcovado National Park, and it was awesome. It takes 3-hours round trip by boat to get there, so it’s extremely isolated, with the Park Rangers stationed there being the only inhabitants. 

Corcovado National Park, on Costa Rica’s remote Osa Peninsula, is often described as one of the most biologically intense places on Earth, offering a rare glimpse of wildlife thriving in an almost completely untouched environment. Its remoteness is a defining feature—most visitors can only access the park by boat or on long, challenging hikes, with the famed Sirena Ranger Station serving as the heart of the experience deep within the rainforest. This isolation protects an extraordinary density of wildlife: all four of Costa Rica’s monkey species, scarlet macaws, herds of peccaries, vibrant poison dart frogs, crocodiles, and larger, harder-to-see species like Baird’s tapirs, giant anteaters, and even jaguars and pumas. The combination of difficult access, vast stretches of primary rainforest, and minimal human presence makes Corcovado not just a national park but one of the last truly wild places in Central America.

Golfo Dulce, located along the eastern edge of Costa Rica’s Osa Peninsula, is one of the world’s only tropical fjords and a sanctuary of extraordinary biodiversity. Enclosed by lush rainforest and calm, warm waters, it serves as a critical habitat for marine life—most famously humpback whales, which gather here from both the Northern and Southern hemispheres to breed and calve. Mangrove forests, coral communities, and quiet inlets support dolphins, sea turtles, and an array of fish species, while the surrounding peninsula hosts some of the most intact lowland rainforest left in Central America. Remote, serene, and ecologically rich, Golfo Dulce is a rare blend of marine and terrestrial wilderness that showcases the pristine beauty of Costa Rica’s southern Pacific coast.

DSkptZ0CXRO.content:
📍🇩🇪 Cologne, Germany 

Cologne’s Christmas markets are inseparable from Glühwein, especially the dramatic Feuerzangenbowle, where a rum-soaked sugar cube is set ablaze and slowly melts into spiced wine below. The markets are filled with comforting winter foods like bratwurst, reibekuchen (crispy potato pancakes), roasted chestnuts, and gingerbread, creating a warm, festive atmosphere. The most famous market sits beside the towering Cologne Cathedral, its lights and wooden stalls framed by one of Europe’s greatest Gothic landmarks. This market draws on centuries-old medieval traditions, reflecting Cologne’s long history as a major religious, trade, and pilgrimage city along the Rhine.

DSndH88iIJn.content:
📍🇧🇪 Brugge, Belgium

Somewhere in my memory is this time I went to Brugge with this other couple about 13 years ago and they fought the whole time, and at one point the wife told the husband to “shut the fuck up.” True story. Other than that, the highlight of that trip was stumbling into De Garre and having this Tripel, it’s seriously the best Tripel I’ve ever had and a must if you love Belgian beer. Brugge is awesome for Christmas, it’s pretty small and not super crowded but also has an incredible old town area, easily one of the best in Europe. 

Brugge is a beautifully preserved medieval city whose canals, guild houses, and cobblestone streets reflect its peak as a powerful Hanseatic trading hub in the 13th–15th centuries. At Christmas, the historic Markt square transforms with festive lights and markets set against Gothic architecture, giving the city a storybook atmosphere. Traditional winter foods include rich Flemish stews, waffles, speculoos, and fresh chocolates, often paired with local Trappist and abbey beers or hot spiced jenever. The blend of deep history, candlelit streets, and seasonal flavors makes Brugge especially enchanting during the holidays.

DSpuVnWkSLj.content:
📍🇧🇪 Ghent, Belgium

Ghent is a solid place to spend an afternoon on Christmas Eve. 

Ghent is a historic Flemish city known for its medieval architecture, winding canals, and powerful role as a trade and textile center in the Middle Ages. Landmarks like Gravensteen Castle and St. Bavo’s Cathedral reflect centuries of prosperity and cultural influence. At Christmas, Ghent transforms with festive lights and markets that blend historic charm with cozy winter traditions. The Christmas markets are especially loved for warm treats like freshly fried beignets and indulgent melted raclette sandwiches enjoyed against the backdrop of the old city.

DSscMCjiCGz.content:
📍🇧🇪 Antwerp, Belgium 

Merry Christmas from the City of Diamonds, Antwerp, Belgium. 

At Christmastime, Antwerp glows with warmth and tradition, especially around the Cathedral of Our Lady, where festive markets fill the historic squares with lights, mulled wine, and the scent of waffles. The cathedral itself, a UNESCO World Heritage site, anchors the city’s medieval heart and reflects Antwerp’s golden age as one of Europe’s most important trading ports. Antwerp has been at the heart of the global diamond trade for over 500 years, dating back to the early 15th century, and today nearby districts still handle the majority of the world’s rough and polished diamonds. This blend of seasonal charm, Gothic grandeur, and commercial legacy gives Antwerp a uniquely luminous atmosphere during the holidays.

DSztpQyEbb_.content:
📍🇳🇱 Amsterdam, Netherlands 

Sometimes I just put on music and wander around with no particular plans or direction in mind. I’ll stop for coffee or lunch, maybe taste 6 different cheese stores samples. Before you realize you’ve walked 25-miles through Amsterdam in 2-days. 

Amsterdam rose to prominence in the late Middle Ages and especially during the 17th-century Dutch Golden Age as one of the world’s most important trading cities. As the hub of the Dutch East India Company and home to the world’s first modern stock exchange, it helped pioneer global trade, finance, and capitalism. From Amsterdam, Dutch commercial power extended to colonized and controlled territories including Indonesia (the Dutch East Indies), parts of the Caribbean such as Curaçao and Aruba, Suriname in South America, trading posts in India and Sri Lanka, the Cape Colony in South Africa, and New Netherland in North America (including present-day New York City). These colonies and trade networks allowed Amsterdam to shape global commerce by linking Europe to Asia, Africa, and the Americas.

DS0Gm2uCCoN.content:
📍🇩🇪🇧🇪🇳🇱🎅🏻🎄

If there is one trip I’d recommend for a kid, it’s Europe during the Christmas Market season. It just feels exactly like what Christmas is supposed to feel like, and it’s simply magical for them. We hit Cologne 🇩🇪 Brugge, Ghent, Antwerp 🇧🇪 and Amsterdam 🇳🇱 over 10-days, all great and each offering something slightly different and special. I’ve been to about 25 different Christmas Markets, and hands down Prague, Czech Republic 🇨🇿 is my favorite. It’s the only one I’ve done twice, it is simply perfect. After that, in no particular order, these are my other favorites: Vienna, Austria 🇦🇹 Strasbourg, France 🇫🇷 Ansbach and Nuremberg, Germany 🇩🇪 Budapest, Hungary 🇭🇺

Christmas markets in Europe trace their origins to the late Middle Ages, when winter fairs in German-speaking lands allowed towns to stock up on food and crafts before Christmas; over centuries, these markets evolved into seasonal celebrations of light, warmth, and local identity. What makes them special is how each city expresses the same tradition through its own food and atmosphere: in Nuremberg, the air is filled with the smell of Nürnberger bratwurst and Lebkuchen; nearby Ansbach, rooted in Franconian beer culture, pairs its intimate baroque square with hearty sausages and dark winter beers, often including smoked Rauchbier. Strasbourg, often called the “Capital of Christmas,” reflects Alsatian heritage with flammekueche, bredele cookies, and spiced vin chaud, while Vienna’s imperial markets emphasize refinement, offering punsch, roasted chestnuts, sausages, and pastries beneath grand architecture. In Prague, Gothic backdrops frame stalls selling trdelník, ham roasted on spits, and hot mead, creating a medieval feel, while Budapest blends Central European flavors with lángos, goulash, chimney cake, and mulled wine along the Danube. Together, these markets transform winter into a shared ritual—where regional food, history, and community turn cold nights into something festive.

DVMkbZEkRow.content:
📍🇨🇴 Medellín, Colombia 

Enjoy this time lapse as a storm rolls in over the mountains. 

Medellín is Colombia’s second-largest city, nestled in the lush Aburrá Valley and known as the “City of Eternal Spring” for its mild, year-round climate. Once infamous for cartel violence associated with Pablo Escobar in the 1980s and early 1990s, Medellín has since transformed into one of Latin America’s most innovative urban centers. The city is celebrated for its pioneering public transportation system—especially its cable cars connecting hillside neighborhoods—vibrant street art in Comuna 13, thriving tech and startup scene, and rich paisa culture. Visitors are drawn to landmarks like Plaza Botero, filled with sculptures by hometown artist Fernando Botero, as well as the city’s lively food scene, coffee culture, and annual Flower Festival (Feria de las Flores).

DVRmaW_kez7.content:
📍🇨🇴 Medellín, Colombia

Colombia is special, it’s rare for me to visit anywhere twice, I’ve only done it for Mexico and Costa Rica in Latin America, but the country just had so much to offer. I think South America is just this constant state of contradictions; it’s chaotic and laid back all at the same time. When I came here in 2015, everyone asked the same question “Is it safe?”, it’s a fair question, but very outdated, Pablo Escobar has been dead since 1993, and the issues stemming from him have been over for decades. Once you realize that you’ll understand Colombia has a lot to offer; natural beauty, vibrant cities, incredible food and culture, and amazing people.

Colombia is a vibrant South American country shaped by a complex history that blends Indigenous civilizations, Spanish colonization beginning in the 16th century, independence led by figures like Simón Bolívar, and a more recent era marked by internal conflict and remarkable economic and cultural resurgence. Its culture reflects a rich fusion of Indigenous, African, and Spanish influences, expressed through music such as cumbia and vallenato, colorful festivals, and a deep sense of regional pride. Colombian cuisine is hearty and diverse—dishes like arepas, bandeja paisa, ajiaco, and fresh Caribbean seafood showcase local ingredients ranging from Andean potatoes to tropical plantains. The capital, Bogotá, sits high in the Andes and serves as the political and cultural heart of the nation, known for its historic La Candelaria district and world-class museums. Medellín, once infamous for cartel violence, has transformed into an innovative, forward-looking city celebrated for its eternal spring climate and urban development. On the Caribbean coast, Cartagena enchants visitors with its colonial walled city, vibrant plazas, and centuries-old fortifications, standing as a testament to Colombia’s strategic importance during the Spanish Empire.

DWd7g3xkzLh.content:
📍🇯🇵 Tokyo, Japan

We had a lot of fun in Tokyo, it’s hard to comprehend how big it is, you can ride the subway for 30 minutes and only be a few neighborhoods over from where you started. 

Tokyo’s cherry blossom season, which typically peaks between late March and early April, transforms the city into a sea of pink and white, centered around iconic “hanami” (flower-viewing) spots like Ueno Park, Shinjuku Gyoen, and the Meguro River. This tradition dates back to the Heian period (794–1185), when it was initially an aristocratic pastime before spreading to the common people during the Edo period. Major locations like Ueno Park became famous after the third Tokugawa shogun, Iemitsu, transplanted trees there from Mount Yoshino, while the rows of cherry trees along the Sumida River were reportedly planted by the eighth shogun, Yoshimune, to both provide a public recreation space and help reinforce the riverbanks through the footsteps of visitors. Today, these historical sites remain at the heart of the season, showcasing the Somei-yoshino variety, which was actually developed in Tokyo’s own Somei village in the mid-19th century, as a fleeting symbol of renewal and the ephemeral nature of life.

DWiPePFEVXq.content:
📍🇯🇵 Kyoto, Japan

The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove in Kyoto offers a surreal experience where towering stalks of green bamboo create a natural cathedral, filtering sunlight into a soft, ethereal glow that dance across the forest floor. At the northern edge of the grove lies Tenryu-ji Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site founded in 1339 by the shogun Ashikaga Takauji to venerate Gautama Buddha and appease the spirit of Emperor Go-Daigo. The area’s history is deeply rooted in the Heian Period (794–1185), when it served as a favored retreat for Japanese aristocrats who sought the tranquil beauty of the Oi River and the surrounding mountains. Today, the “Sound of the Bamboo” the rhythmic creaking and rustling of the stalks, is officially recognized by the Japanese Ministry of Environment as one of the 100 Soundscapes of Japan, preserving the spiritual and historical stillness that has defined Arashiyama for centuries.

DWiyH1AkUqG.content:
📍🇯🇵 Kyoto, Japan

Today our guide taught us the Japanese concept of “ichi-go ichi-e” which translates to “one lifetime, one encounter,” serving as a reminder that every single moment and gathering is entirely unique and can never be replicated. To come to Kyoto during cherry blossoms season really captures this for me, it’s incredibly crowded but you can only truly have this experience in this one week window, and it will never be exactly the same even if you came back. Right before we left I saw an article from Travel and Leisure saying “skip Kyoto and go here instead” for Cherry Blossom. Who writes this shit? That’s like saying “skip going to the Super Bowl and go watch the local high school play”. Even if you didn’t come during cherry blossom season Kyoto is a 10/10, I plan to come back to Japan at some point and see everywhere else, but this was an incredible experience.

DSVPBetCeW5.content:
The Non-Negotiables

1) Treat every firearm as if it were loaded 
2) Never point the firearm at anything you do not intend to shoot 
3) Keep you’re finger straight and off the trigger until you’re ready to fire 
4) Know your target and what lies beyond it and in between it

If you’ve trained with me before, you know every class starts with an extensive safety brief. That’s intentional. Safety is Paramount, Safety is Priority No 1.

If you’re looking to learn in a professional, structured, and safety-focused environment, come check out a class and see the difference for yourself.

4 years ago, I lost a brother.
Santiago Sanchez (1985–2022)

We were both wresting team captains at St. John Bosco—
Me at 145 lbs & Santiago at 215 lbs. Me, my teammates, and my Coach Omar came together for his funeral 3 years ago.

but we lived by the same code (which we both quoted in our 2003 high school yearbook):
“It’s not about the size of the dog in the fight… it’s about the size of the fight in the dog.”

And Santiago had more fight—and more loyalty—than anyone I’ve ever known.

He didn’t just have my back…HE SAVED MY LIFE - In a fight in Compton in 2003 when I had to defend myself and I was outnumbered, and things could’ve ended very differently—but Santiago stepped in and saved my life without hesitation. 

That’s not a friend. That’s family.

I owe him—and his family—forever. I recently spoke with his younger brother who is a deputy sheriff, and he inquired about the campaign since we still share the same values. 

As life goes on, people change.
Some walk away when you stand on your beliefs. My wrestling teammates never left. Some college friends did—when I stopped staying quiet about my beliefs and I got closer to God.

But your real brothers?
They never leave.

My wrestling teammates were never just teammates.
They were my family, and they are still my family to this date...

Rest easy, Santi.
Never forgotten. 🙏✝️

Protest attire tip.
Some pants/workwear have pockets at the knees designed for knee pad inserts. This is usually a more comfortable methods for prolonged use of knee pads opposed to the traditional elastic strap knee pads. If your pants don't have the pockets you can always add them. Comfortability is not the top priority but easy changes like this can keep support, medics safe and less distracted by discomfort allowing them to help more effectively. #protest #attire #safety #protestsafety #abolishice

Varje gång jag gjort klart en teckning tänker jag ”hur fan gjorde jag det där?”
Jag som inte ens kan teckna.
Det känns så - jag har ingen aning om vad jag håller på med, tecknar inte av objekt, jag känner mer som att jag avbildar former och mönster i olika färger och när jag är klar har det blivit en bild, eller en avbildning av något.

Jag var 15,eller 16 när jag började med konst, fast jag tycker inte om att säga att jag gör konst, jag var extremt skoltrött och ville ingenting. Men det var ju det där med gymnasiet, man måste ju plugga vidare och bli något.
Min morsa, som själv drömde om att måla, teckna, skriva och skapa, men som pga livet aldrig kunde göra det ”på riktigt”, mer eller mindre tvingade mig att söka till Bild o Form i Hässleholm där vi bodde då.
Hon förstod att jag inte behövde mer av den vanliga skolan och hon såg till att jag fick ihop de arbetsprover som behövdes. Jag kan inte tänka mig att de var särskilt bra…men jag kom in på skolan.
Och det ändrade allt.
Det var 1991 och jag har fortsatt teckna sedan dess, mer eller mindre aktivt, men det har alltid funnits i mitt liv.
Och det är jag oändligt tacksam för.

När jag bodde i usa startade jag ett konto på Patreon, jag var extremt dålig på att använda det, men nu har jag aktiverat det igen och kommer lägga upp lite allt möjligt; små filmer, musik, texter och teckningar.

Länk finns i min bio här ovanför.

Instagram känns mer och mer dött och framförallt verkar det helt omöjligt att nå ut till folk, efter 10 år på den här plattformen är det oftast bara ett 20-tal personer som gillar eller ser mina inlägg.
Om du tycker om det jag gör och tycker det är värt att stötta så kan du bli prenumerant (60kr i månaden) och få en lite mer personlig inblick i vad jag gör.
Dessutom får prenumeranter möjlighet att köpa teckningar före alla andra, samt till ett lägre pris.

Jag är trött på idén att allt som musiker och andra kreativa gör förväntas vara tillgängligt gratis (don’t get me started om hur Spotify tex drar in biljoner på andras arbete).
Det ligger tusentals timmar och många år av arbete bakom den färdiga ”produkten”; övning, slit, misslyckanden och passion, dedikation och envishet. Det jag (och andra som jag) gör, ”händer” inte bara av sig självt. 
Jag har lagt en massa pengar på utrustning och material, jag har kånkat instrument på alla möjliga tider och platser, jag har drömt, planerat, försökt och försökt igen, jag har skrivit och skrivit om, tecknat och målat, sjungit och spelat i drygt 30 år utan att knappt tjäna en spänn…
Så. Nu kör jag på Patreon och ni är varmt välkomna att följa mig där.
Jag kommer fortsätta lägga upp bilder här också, men kanske inte lika frekvent och det jag lägger upp här kommer upp först på Patreon.

Allt det där vi växte upp med, alla fina ord om ”aldrig igen” och alla människors lika värde osv osv…det var bara tomma ord.

DRUTwPrCGAK.content:
Idag släpps tredje singeln från kommande albumet med @ior_gbg 

Nattryttare.

Efter att ha levt alldeles för länge med huvudet böjt, kom jag äntligen tillbaks till livet och öste ur mig allt jag kände i låt efter låt. En dag tog det slut. Tvärt. Det var som att orden försvann, som att allting hade blivit nedtecknat som var tvunget att komma ut.
Jag blundade och såg alla drömmar som små lysande pärlor, uppträdda på trådar som sträckte sig över tid och rum.
På nyårsaftonen satt jag vid pianot och hörde någon sjunga svagt på parkeringen nedanför, jag hörde inte orden, men melodin i all sin enkelhet fyllde mig med lugn. Jag var inte längre den som hukade mig, jag var fri och stark och lycklig och vi såg fyrverkerierna explodera ett par timmar senare och jag visste att jag aldrig mer ska låta mig själv försvinna så som jag gjorde.

DTdoTX-CY49.content:
1960: One job. One income.
A house. A car. A vacation.
Mom stayed home. Dad clocked out at 5 and actually rested.
Life wasn’t fancy... but it was doable.
2025: Two full-time incomes.
Still can’t afford rent, childcare, health insurance, or a break.
Parents are exhausted. Kids are growing up watching us scramble.
And everyone keeps saying, “This is just how life is now.”
But let’s be honest...
Most families would trade everything for the version of “normal” our grandparents had.
Less chaos. More margin. More family dinners.
More peace.
And it’s heartbreaking that what used to be standard now feels like a distant fantasy.
Families aren’t asking for luxury - they’re asking for a life that doesn’t require sacrificing their health, marriage, or time with their kids just to survive.
We’re not broken.
The system is. 
#metoofamilycourt #mrdoubtfire #debtbeatdad #strongasamother #legalizefatherhood

DV7jpsXESqX.content:
50yrs THIS WEEK….Normally i would whinge about being so old but when i look back on my youth i have lived through some of THE most prosperous decades of rock n’ roll that are NEVER to be repeated so i CANT complain…Like THIS week !!! On March 15, 1976, the New York quartet released Destroyer, their fourth studio album and the record that transformed them from cult, live circuit favorites into arena-conquering legends. Half a century later, Rolling Stone (i WAS a good rag back then), STILL ranks it among the 500 greatest albums of all time, and the fans who grew up with it couldn’t agree more.

The timing of Destroyer was everything. Three years of relentless touring and theatrical live shows had built a fanatical following, but it was the band’s 1975 live album Alive!, which spent 110 weeks on the Billboard chart and became their first gold-certified record, that finally cracked open the mainstream. Riding that momentum, KISS turned to producer Bob Ezrin, fresh off his acclaimed work with Alice Cooper, to help them make their most ambitious studio record yet. The lineup reads like a greatest-hits collection all on its own: the thunderous “God of Thunder,” the anthemic “Shout It Out Loud” and the soft-rock ballad “Beth,” which became the band’s first top-10 single, peaking at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100. Destroyer itself peaked at No. 11 on the Billboard 200 and was eventually certified double platinum by the RIAA, the first KISS album to reach that milestone. For ME it was their PEAK everything….Popularity, performance & presence !!! Introducing their ICONIC Kiss Alive II stage set-up, which was a FIRST of its kind AND of course their iconic outfits…..!!!! This was them at their biggest & fucking best. That era marked them as the BIGGEST band in music & the atmosphere at that time was magnetic….WHAT A TIME !!!!! My fav standout tracks are Sweet Pain & Flaming Youth ⭐️ #rockandroll #rock #metal #kiss #beer ☠️☠️☠️

DWiRr0pkX1P.content: For a debut this shows incredible potential for whats ahead. A brilliantly morbid & brooding story. A young woman finds herself at odds with her neighbours in a remote community of religious fanatics, led by her father, the town Pastor.  With her abusive husband having been killed under mysterious circumstances, Magpie is already an outcast. When another monstrous man turns up dead after a run-in with Magpie, she finds herself the prime suspect – never mind the white-eyed horned beast lurking in the woods. You never really find out what this creature is or what it wants but it looks frightfully devil like & just downright horrible….While not a plot line breaking any new ground, its shot with such an effective simplicity & the soundtrack & noise-scapes they create blend eerily with the story AND its location. Thoroughly enjoyed this ☠️ #film #filmphotography #movie #drama #horror 🎥

DWsMNihiYvq.content: Let me start by stressing THIS is the NEW Bodycam 2026 film just released on Shudder (as there are at least 3 other movies of the same name-not related). MY GOD this thing was pure nightmare fuel for me the second it commenced & i mean that LITERALLY !! No credits at all at the beginning just the title & BAM stra8 into it….!! Two officers respond to what SHOULD be a regular DV call-out to a decrepit, crackhouse neighbourhood…Not an unusual thing. But within minutes all descends into a total claustrophobic, demented & DEMONIC fucking shit show…..!! The first 20mins in particular are difficult to watch. More to the story unravels as it moves along building to a pretty horrific ending for ALL involved….! Its a low budget but SO brilliantly portrayed. Hats off to the director as this really shows what you can pull off with no budget at all. Incredibly tense, unsettling, the gore is brutal & on point without being over ridiculous-which kind of makes it all the more unnerving. 8/10 !!!! A VERY decent watch for Found Footage fans……☠️ #film #filmphotography #movie #horror #beer 🔪
